entries.opinion: To me, this movie is about staying true to yourself while still achieving remarkable things. In today's world, that feels increasingly difficult. We often measure success by ambition, competition, and personal gain, but *Forrest Gump* reminds us that kindness, sincerity, and integrity are not weaknesses—they are strengths. It suggests that true success is not only about what we accomplish, but also about the person we choose to remain throughout the journey. Being both kind and successful is rare, and that is what makes Forrest's story so inspiring.

recommendTo: people who is struggling with his life
entries.opinion: His life journey is showing how everything is not that diffucult. It is easy to complicate and that is what we usually do. In general his achievements are not about status and wealth, in general it can be simple human relationships. If you figure out simple mechanics of the things in life and you can do whatever you want. It seems like that mechanic can be discovered to specific person.

To me, the film was never primarily about revenge or even escaping prison. After all, even once Andy had escaped, he still had opportunities to pursue revenge if that had been his true motivation. Instead, I saw the prison as a metaphor for the invisible prisons we create within our own minds. The story suggests that genuine freedom is impossible without first confronting and redeeming ourselves. We must recognize the psychological or emotional prisons that confine us before we can find a way out. Only after that process of self-discovery and redemption can we experience true freedom, regardless of our physical circumstances.
